title: The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 (Part XVI & XVI-A: ASU Drugs)
authority: Ministry of Ayush / State Licensing Authorities
issuing_body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / Ministry of Ayush

provisions.heading: Guidelines for Issue of License with Respect to Patent or Proprietary ASU Medicine
provisions.text:
For the grant of license for Patent or Proprietary ASU medicines under Rule 154:
(I) For ASU medicines containing ingredients mentioned in the First Schedule books with new indications, proof of safety and effectiveness based on textual rationales or pilot clinical trial data is required.
(II) For ASU medicines with modified extracts or novel extraction techniques, acute toxicity studies and published scientific literature are required.
(III) For novel botanical combinations not in classical texts, safety data and clinical trial verification as prescribed are required.

location.part: Part XVI (Manufacture for Sale of ASU Drugs)

provisions.statutory_significance: The exact evidentiary threshold for state licensing of proprietary Ayurvedic drugs.

provisions.heading: Labelling, Packing and Batch Details
provisions.text:
Every container of an Ayurvedic drug shall bear on its label:
(a) Name of the drug (classical name as per First Schedule, or proprietary brand name).
(b) Complete list of all ingredients with their Sanskrit botanical names and quantities.
(c) The name of the classical text (for classical drugs).
(d) Batch number, manufacturing license number, manufacturing date, and expiry date.
(e) Prominent warning for Schedule E(1) ingredients: 'To be taken under medical supervision'.

location.part: Part XVII (Labelling and Packing of ASU Drugs)

provisions.statutory_significance: Mandatory statutory labelling checklist for retail commercialization.

provisions.heading: Good Manufacturing Practices for Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Medicines
provisions.text: Prescribes factory requirements for location, premises, hygiene, raw material quarantine, manufacturing records (BMR), standard operating procedures, and quality control laboratories.
provisions.statutory_significance: Prerequisite for manufacturing license issuance and international WHO-GMP export certification.

provisions.heading: Definition of Phytopharmaceutical Drug & Clinical Trial Requirements
provisions.text: A phytopharmaceutical drug is defined as a purified and standardized fraction with defined minimum four bioactive or analytical markers of an extract of a medicinal plant or its part, for internal or external use of human beings or animals for diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of any disease or disorder, but does not include administration by parenteral route. Requires regulatory approval from CDSCO on Form CT-18 with human phase II and phase III clinical trials under Schedule Y / New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules.
provisions.statutory_significance: Modern scientific botanical drug approval pathway under CDSCO.

provisions.heading: Conditions for the Grant or Renewal of a License in Form 25D
provisions.text: Before a license in Form 25D is granted or renewed, the licensing authority must satisfy itself that the manufacture shall be conducted under the active direction and personal supervision of competent technical staff and that the premises comply with Good Manufacturing Practices prescribed in Schedule T.
provisions.statutory_significance: Statutory prerequisite tying manufacturing licenses to Schedule T GMP.
